Hi Linda —

Thanks — we can provide the material and a short runbook that maps each storage surface to retention and erase steps. High level summary below; detailed artifacts (retention matrix CSV, runbook PDF, and a scrub log sample) attached.

Summary: 
- Region pinning: customers on Dedicated can pin a tenant to a single cloud region; compute instances and persistent block storage remain in-region.
- Backups & snapshots: periodic snapshots are configurable; default is in-region retention with optional cross-region replication only under explicit contract.
- Transient caches (KV cache, prefix caches) are in-memory on pinned hosts; for longer-lived caches persisted to local SSDs we scrub on teardown.
- Delete/erasure flow: tenant deletion -> immediate revocation of routing -> snapshot retention check -> background purge job that removes live data and marks snapshots for deletion -> snapshot GC after retention period; we provide a wipe evidence bundle once purge completes. Typical complete evidence turnaround: 7–14 days (dependent on snapshot replication cadence).

I’ve attached: 20261026-region-pin-runbook.pdf (runbook + mapping), 20261026-retention-matrix.csv (by surface), and a sample wipe evidence log. Karthik and Marissa are CC’d to add the deeper technical notes and a proposed SLA for evidence delivery.

Next steps: Karthik will confirm the default snapshots cadence and exact timelines for offsite backup retention, and Marissa will confirm a format for the attestation we can provide. Happy to jump on a quick call if you prefer.

Best,
Jordan Blake

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: geolocation evidence + retention matrix for Dedicated deployment

Linda / Jordan —

Adding technical detail for FinWell’s review. I’ll keep this pragmatic.

What region pinning covers (explicit):
- Compute: instances that run inference are scheduled only on the pinned region's hosts. There is a != scheduling constraint in our orchestrator that prevents placement outside the pinned region.
- Persistent volumes: block storage (encrypted at rest) is provisioned in the pinned region and mounted to the tenant’s hosts.
- Object backups/snapshots: by default, snapshots are stored in the same region. Cross-region replication is an opt-in feature requiring a signed request and dedicated replication policy.

Storage surfaces and retention (defaults):
- Live tenant DB (metadata & pointers): retained until tenant deletion + purge process (retention: N/A — live until delete).
- Persistent snapshots: configurable; default retention 30 days before eligible for GC.
- Backup exports (manual/managed export to object store): retained per customer config; default 90 days only if enabled.
- Audit logs: stored for 180 days by default in our logging cluster (we can extend on contract).
- KV/prefix cache: in-memory; on host restart we invalidate. For any persisted on-local-SSD caches we run a multi-pass overwrite during teardown before host reclamation.

Deletion / erasure workflow (sequence):
1) Submit tenant decommission request (API or Console).
2) Immediate routing revocation and access token revocation (minutes).
3) Mark tenant for purge and schedule background jobs: live object deletion + snapshot marking (hours).
4) Snapshot GC: eligible snapshots are removed after configured retention window; GC process deletes objects and updates metadata stores (asynchronous).
5) Evidence bundle generation: once object delete and metadata update succeed, we produce a hash-signed log bundle that includes delete operation IDs, object keys removed, and storage-level confirmations (typically 7–14 days for default snapshot cadence).

Notes on cross-region replication: we do not replicate customer objects or snapshots across regions unless explicitly configured. Replication is a policy-level opt-in that requires a signed configuration and will be surfaced in the runbook and contract.

Artifacts we can provide to FinWell: 
- Retention matrix CSV (per-surface) — included
- Runbook PDF showing operator steps and CLI commands — included
- Sample signed wipe evidence log and a canonical schema for the evidence — included
- If required, we can provide a one-off live demo of the purge flow in a dedicated staging tenant and share the real-time logs.

Open items / items for FinWell decision: 
- Snapshot retention policy to be finalized (we can set to 0 days eligible for immediate GC if they require immediate deletion but that impacts rollback/restore capabilities).
- Audit log retention beyond 180 days — contract amendment required.

Happy to attach a suggested SLA clause for evidence delivery; Jordan, I’ll hand this to Marissa for the attestation template.

—Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Jordan / Karthik —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. A few clarifying questions from our SOC team: 

1) When you say 'hash-signed log bundle' — can you specify the signature scheme and whether we can independently verify the signatures? We need cryptographic assurance (e.g., signing cert + chain).
2) If a tenant requests immediate destruction, and we set snapshots to be eligible immediately, what is the realistic wall-clock time until the S3/object-store level objects are gone and we can receive evidence? Is that still 7–14 days or can it be shorter?
3) Are there any third-party backups (for disaster recovery) that might retain copies outside the pinned region unintentionally (e.g., monitoring or support artifacts stored in a central analytics cluster)?

Also: if you can provide a sample of the actual 'evidence bundle' format (schema + sanitized sample) and an operator checklist that the compliance board can follow, that will help accelerate procurement.

—Linda

(attachment: soc-review-questions.docx)

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Linda Park <linda.park@finwell.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-30T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: geolocation evidence + retention matrix for Dedicated deployment

Linda —

Appreciate the clear ask. Final deliverables and answers below, and I’ve attached the requested sanitized sample evidence bundle and a short operator checklist.

Answers: 
- Signature scheme: we sign evidence bundles with our platform signing key using RSA-2048 and SHA-256; bundles include the signing cert and full chain so FinWell can independently verify. We can also offer HSM-backed signing on dedicated contracts if required.
- Wall-clock for immediate destruction: if you set snapshots to be eligible immediately, object deletions start within the next GC run. For standard GC cadence the conservative estimate is 7 days; with accelerated GC/expedited plan we can target 48–72 hours to produce evidence (subject to no replication backlog). We’ll include an SLA addon for the expedited timeline if you require it.
- Third-party retention: we do not copy tenant object data to central analytics or multi-tenant clusters by default. Non-sensitive telemetry (anonymized metrics) may go to central clusters; we will list exact artifact types and ensure nothing that contains tenant objects is replicated. Support-access recordings or escalations are recorded as case notes; they do not include raw tenant objects.

Deliverables attached: 
- 20261030-region-pin-runbook.pdf (operator steps + pinned-host assertions)
- 20261030-retention-matrix.csv (canonical mapping and configurable fields)
- 20261030-wipe-evidence-sample.log (signed sample bundle)
- operator-checklist.txt (sanitized step-by-step for compliance reviewers)

Next step: Jordan to open a support ticket for the accelerated GC option if FinWell wants the 48–72 hour SLA. Karthik and Marissa can be looped for the attestation and contract clause. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough of the bundle on Tuesday.

Best,
